questions.question: Name the five line types used in Grade 9 technical drawing and state what each represents.
questions.expected_answer: Dark continuous outline for visible edges; feint continuous construction line for setting out and projecting between views; medium dashed line for hidden detail, edges behind a surface; freehand wavy break line where part of a long object is left out; chain line, long dash short dash, thin for centre lines and paths of movement and thick-ended with arrows for a cutting plane that produces a section.

questions.question: A ramp is 7 200 millimetres long and 1 200 millimetres wide. Show how you would choose a scale to fit it on an A4 page and give the drawing sizes.
questions.expected_answer: Choose a standard scale, the largest that fits with room for dimensions and the title block. At 1:50 the length is 7 200 divided by 50, which is 144 millimetres, and the width is 1 200 divided by 50, which is 24 millimetres; this fits on an A4 page of 297 by 210 millimetres. At 1:20 the length would be 360 millimetres, too long, so 1:50 is chosen and written in the title block. Dimensions on the drawing still state 7 200 and 1 200.

questions.question: State the four parts of a dimension and four rules for placing dimensions on a working drawing.
questions.expected_answer: Parts: extension lines projecting from the edges with a small gap from the object, a dimension line parallel to the edge, arrowheads or oblique strokes at its ends, and the number in millimetres without a unit above the line. Rules: place dimensions outside the outline; give each size once in the view that shows it most clearly; put overall sizes outside smaller ones; avoid crossing dimension and extension lines and never write a number on a line; dimensions always give real sizes, not scaled sizes.
